questions.scenario: Your team processes 10,000 customer service emails per day, each requiring a brief, friendly acknowledgment. The emails are simple and straightforward. Which model should you start with?
questions.a: Opus, because it's the most capable and your customers deserve the best.
questions.b: Haiku, because these are short, simple jobs at high volume where speed and cost matter most.
questions.c: Sonnet, because it balances capability and cost evenly.
questions.d: Whichever is fastest on any given day, since volume is unpredictable.
questions.why: The job matches Haiku's profile: short, simple, high-volume work where speed and cost are the priorities. The lesson explicitly recommends Haiku for this type of job.
questions.quote: Short, simple jobs at volume, where speed and cost matter most

questions.scenario: A researcher needs to analyze one highly technical 100-page academic paper to identify potential flaws in the methodology. The accuracy of the analysis is critical, and time is not a constraint. Which model best fits this job?
questions.a: Haiku, to save tokens and complete the analysis quickly.
questions.b: Sonnet, as the everyday default that balances speed and capability.
questions.c: Opus, because complex reasoning is needed and accuracy outweighs the cost.
questions.d: Any model, since a single-use job doesn't multiply costs.
questions.why: This is a one-off job where quality and accuracy are everything. The lesson recommends Opus for scenarios where complex reasoning is required and being right outweighs cost considerations.
questions.quote: Complex reasoning, where being right outweighs the cost
